Cu partitioning

Vertical pH-only boundaries in the dissolved Cu(II) region (E-independent) occur where two complexes swap dominance. Horizontal / diagonal boundaries between oxidation states follow the conditional Nernst potentials in §2.

  • pH 0 – 3.25: Cu²⁺ is the dominant dissolved Cu(II) form (chloride complexes never rise above ≈20 %).
  • pH 3.25 – 4.25: switches to Cu(gly)⁺. Boundary set by log β₁(Gly) + log αGly⁻(pH) = 0 → pH ≈ 3.25.
  • pH 4.25 – 5.35: transient CuCit⁻ window (citrate becomes fully deprotonated near pH 6.4; below the second glycine deprotonation, citrate wins).
  • pH 5.35 – 11.65: Cu(gly)₂ dominates a very wide field (log β₂ = 15.6; two Gly⁻ arms make it the strongest 2:1 complex here).
  • pH 11.65 – 13.90: Cu(OH)₂(s) precipitates because [Cu²⁺]free demanded by Cu(gly)₂ falls below the Ksp threshold. Solver junction: pH 11.65 (Cu(gly)₂ · Cu(OH)₂), pH 13.90 (redissolution to Cu(OH)₄²⁻).
  • Cu(I) speciation: CuCl₂⁻ below pH 6.7, Cu(NH₃)₂⁺ above. The field only spans −0.03 V ≲ E ≲ +0.12 V and shrinks continuously with pH; above pH ≈ 7 the Cu(II)/Cu(I) formal potential drops below the Cu(I)/Cu(0) formal potential and Cu(I) is thermodynamically eliminated by disproportionation.

  • pH 1.25 – 4.60: FeCit(aq) (log β = 13.1). Citrate wins as soon as even 1 % of it is in the Cit³⁻ form (~pH 1.5).
  • pH 4.60 – 6.10: Fe(OH)Cit⁻ takes over (log β for Fe³⁺+Cit³⁻+OH⁻ = 22.3, so the switch is at pH such that log βOHcit + log[OH⁻] = log βCit, i.e. pH = pKw + (13.1 − 22.3) = 4.58).
  • pH 6.10 – 10.60: Fe(OH)₂Cit²⁻; same argument applied twice.

  • Fe(II) speciation: Fe²⁺ (pH ≤ 4.5) → FeCit⁻ (4.5–9.25) → Fe(gly)₂ (9.25–11.7).
  • Fe(OH)₂(s) opens at pH ≈ 9.4 for Fe(II) at 1 mM; the Fe(II)–glycine complex is not strong enough (log β₂ = 7.7) to keep it dissolved.
  • Fe(III)/Fe(II) formal potential: shifted from +0.771 V to +0.056 V at pH 7 — a 715 mV cathodic shift due to the ~10¹²× stronger Fe(III) complexation by citrate compared with Fe(II). Above pH ≈ 8 it drops below H₂O/H₂, so every Fe(III) present will be autoreduced by any mild reducer in an ammoniacal-citrate bath.
  • Fe(s) upper boundary: sits at ≈ −0.54 V at low pH, drifts to −0.85 V at pH 14; almost coincident with H₂O/H₂ from pH ≈ 10 on, so Fe deposition is inseparable from parasitic H₂ evolution above pH ≈ 10.

The right panel is the intersection of the two metallic regions. The gap between the two metal-plating lines is the practical figure of merit for Cu–Fe alloy plating.

Key observations for the electrolyte designer:

  • Even with all four ligands acting on Cu(II) (chloride, ammonia, glycine, citrate), the smallest Cu–Fe deposition gap is about ~550 mV at pH 10. That is small enough for iron-rich Fe–Cu alloys to be deposited from a single bath, but Fe deposition sits right at the H₂O/H₂ line, so current efficiency will be limited by co-evolving H₂.
  • The commonly used tactic — ammine complexation to depress the Cu potential — is only partially effective here. Above pH ≈ 8 the four Cu(gly)₂ arms overwhelm the four Cu(NH₃)₄²⁺ arms because the free NH₃ activity is limited by the NH₄⁺/NH₃ equilibrium (αNH₃(pH 8) ≈ 0.05), while Gly⁻ is nearly fully deprotonated already at pH ≈ 8.5.
  • Fe(III) is very effectively sequestered by citrate: over pH 2 – 6.9 no Fe(OH)₃ forms and Fe(III) sits entirely as FeCit / Fe(OH)Cit⁻. Above pH ≈ 7 the Fe(OH)₃(s,am) field opens; the user's exclusion of Fe₂O₃ / FeOOH / Fe₃O₄ simply keeps that region labelled as the amorphous hydroxide rather than a crystalline oxide.
  • Cu(I) is only observable as an intermediate in a narrow band around E ≈ +0.1 V, and only below pH 8 where CuCl₂⁻ or Cu(NH₃)₂⁺ is strong enough to survive disproportionation. Baths intended to plate through Cu(I) intermediates should therefore be run below pH 6.5 with elevated chloride, or between pH 8 – 10 with elevated free ammonia, and away from the Cu₂O island.

5. Caveats

Approximations kept explicit. (i) Ligand concentrations were treated as analytical × acid-base α, i.e. free-ligand depletion by metal binding was neglected (≤10 % effect at 1 mM metal, 10 mM ligand). (ii) Only mononuclear complexes reported by Smith & Martell / NIST 46 were included; polynuclear hydroxides of Cu and Fe are known to matter only above ~10⁻³ M free metal — that threshold is not reached anywhere on this diagram. (iii) Anhydrous oxides (Fe₂O₃, CuO, FeOOH, Fe₃O₄) were removed per request; their omission is thermodynamically consistent only under fast, water-rich deposition kinetics where the amorphous hydroxide precipitates first and does not dehydrate. (iv) Activity coefficients were not re-applied to the tabulated log β; the values quoted are conditional constants at I ≈ 0.1 m (most already reported at that ionic strength; those originally at I = 0 were Davies-corrected before being written into the table). All conditional potentials reported are direct, unconditional Nernst expressions using those log β.

"""
Speciation for Cu(II)/Ni(II)/Zn(II) selectivity — cyclam, cyclen, trien
Conditions: 1 mM total metal (each), 5 mM total ligand, I = 0.1 M, 25 °C, pH 6-8
SRD-46 / Smith-Martell critically selected log K values.
Fully numerical: solves the mass-balance equations, does not assume "all M bound".
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import brentq

# =========================================================================
# Ligand data (log K for successive protonation, largest first;
# log K for M+L=ML; and for M+H+L=MHL where reliably reported)
# =========================================================================
LIGANDS = {
    "cyclam": {
        "pKa": [11.29, 10.19, 1.61, 2.09],   # succ. protonation, I=0.1
        "logK_ML":  {"Cu": 27.2, "Ni": 22.2, "Zn": 15.5},
        "logK_MHL": {"Cu": None,  "Ni": None,  "Zn": None},   # negligible near neutral
    },
    "cyclen": {
        "pKa": [10.97, 9.87, 1.61, 0.90],
        "logK_ML":  {"Cu": 24.8, "Ni": 16.4, "Zn": 16.2},
        "logK_MHL": {"Cu": None,  "Ni": None,  "Zn": None},
    },
    "trien": {
        "pKa": [9.74, 9.07, 6.56, 3.25],
        "logK_ML":  {"Cu": 20.4, "Ni": 14.0, "Zn": 12.1},
        "logK_MHL": {"Cu": 23.9, "Ni": None,  "Zn": None},   # CuHL reported
    },
}

# Metal hydroxide side reactions (log β for M + n OH^- = M(OH)_n^(2-n))
METAL_OH = {
    "Cu": [6.3, 11.8, 14.5, 15.6],
    "Ni": [4.1, 8.0, 11.0, None],
    "Zn": [5.0, 11.1, 13.6, 14.8],
}

def alpha_L(pH, pKa):
    """α_L(H) = [L']/[L]  — accounts for all protonated free-ligand forms."""
    H = 10**(-pH)
    # pKa list is entered largest-first, so K_H1 = 10**pKa[0] etc.
    a = 1.0
    prod = 1.0
    for pK in pKa:
        prod *= 10**pK * H
        a += prod
    return a

def alpha_M_OH(pH, betas):
    """α_M(OH) = 1 + Σ β_n [OH^-]^n  — hydroxide side reactions."""
    OH = 10**(pH - 14)
    a = 1.0
    for n, logb in enumerate(betas, start=1):
        if logb is not None:
            a += 10**logb * OH**n
    return a

def solve_free_M(M_tot, L_tot, pH, logK_ML, logK_MHL, pKa, betas_OH):
    """
    Solve for [M^2+] given total M, total L, pH.
    Mass balances:
       M_tot = [M^2+]·α_M(OH) + [ML] + [MHL]
       L_tot = [L]·α_L(H)     + [ML] + [MHL]
    with [ML]  = K_ML  · [M^2+] · [L]
         [MHL] = K_MHL · [M^2+] · [L] · [H^+]        (β_MHL = K(M+H+L=MHL))
    Solve numerically for [M^2+].
    """
    H = 10**(-pH)
    K_ML  = 10**logK_ML
    K_MHL = 10**logK_MHL if logK_MHL is not None else 0.0
    aL    = alpha_L(pH, pKa)
    aM    = alpha_M_OH(pH, betas_OH)

    # Effective 1:1 formation constant collecting ML + MHL: 
    #   [ML]+[MHL] = [M^2+][L] (K_ML + K_MHL · [H+])
    Keff = K_ML + K_MHL * H

    def residual(logM):
        M = 10**logM
        # From L balance: L_tot = [L]·aL + Keff·M·[L]  =>  [L] = L_tot/(aL + Keff·M)
        L_free = L_tot / (aL + Keff * M)
        ML_tot = Keff * M * L_free
        return M * aM + ML_tot - M_tot

    # Bracket [M^2+] between 1e-40 and M_tot
    lo, hi = -40.0, np.log10(M_tot) + 0.001
    # ensure sign change
    if residual(lo) * residual(hi) > 0:
        # fallback: coarse scan
        for x in np.linspace(hi, lo, 400):
            if residual(x) < 0:
                hi = x + 0.2
                break
    logM_sol = brentq(residual, lo, hi, xtol=1e-8)
    M = 10**logM_sol
    L_free = L_tot / (aL + Keff * M)
    ML  = K_ML  * M * L_free
    MHL = K_MHL * M * L_free * H
    return {
        "[M2+]": M,

from scipy.optimize import fsolve

# All constants I=0.1 M, 25 °C (approx values from NIST SRD-46 / Martell-Smith Vol.1)

ligands = {
    'Glycine': {
        'pKa': [2.35, 9.78],
        'metals': {
            'Cu': [8.15, 15.03],
            'Ni': [5.72, 10.61, 13.83],
            'Co': [4.60, 8.35, 10.72],
        }
    },
    'L-Histidine': {
        'pKa': [1.70, 6.04, 9.09],
        'metals': {
            'Cu': [10.20, 18.20],
            'Ni': [8.69, 15.53],
            'Co': [6.87, 12.24],
        }
    },
    'L-Aspartate': {
        'pKa': [2.05, 3.87, 9.82],
        'metals': {
            'Cu': [8.57, 14.78],
            'Ni': [7.12, 12.42],
            'Co': [5.90, 10.13],
        }
    },
}

# Cumulative hydroxide constants log β_n for M(OH)_n^(2-n) formed from M2+ + n OH-
hydrolysis = {
    'Cu': [6.3, 11.8, 14.5, 15.6],
    'Ni': [4.1, 8.0, 11.0, 12.0],
    'Co': [4.3, 8.4, 9.7, 10.2],
}

def alpha_L(pH, pKas):
    H = 10**(-pH)
    pk = sorted(pKas)  # ascending pKa (Ka1 largest, i.e. most acidic first)
    # alpha = 1 + sum over adding i protons using the i largest pKas
    a = 1.0
    for i in range(len(pk)):
        logbetaH = sum(pk[-(j+1)] for j in range(i+1))
        a += 10**logbetaH * H**(i+1)
    return a

def alpha_M(pH, log_betas):
    OH = 10**(pH - 14)
    a = 1.0
    for i, lb in enumerate(log_betas):
        a += 10**lb * OH**(i+1)
    return a

def speciate(M_T, L_T, pH, ligand_name, metal):
    L_data = ligands[ligand_name]
    betas = L_data['metals'][metal]
    aL = alpha_L(pH, L_data['pKa'])
    aM = alpha_M(pH, hydrolysis[metal])

    def eqs(v):
        logL, logM = v
        L = 10**logL; M = 10**logM
        S1 = sum(10**betas[i] * L**(i+1) for i in range(len(betas)))       # sum βi L^i
        S2 = sum((i+1) * 10**betas[i] * L**(i+1) for i in range(len(betas)))
        # M mass bal:  M*(aM + S1) = M_T
        # L mass bal:  L*aL + M*S2 = L_T
        return [np.log10(M*(aM + S1)) - np.log10(M_T),
                np.log10(L*aL + M*S2)  - np.log10(L_T)]

    # Initial guess
    x0 = [np.log10(L_T/aL), np.log10(M_T*0.01)]
    sol = fsolve(eqs, x0, full_output=True)
    logL, logM = sol[0]
    L = 10**logL; M = 10**logM
    # Species distribution
    species = {'M2+': M, 'ML': 10**betas[0]*M*L}
    if len(betas) >= 2: species['ML2'] = 10**betas[1]*M*L**2
    if len(betas) >= 3: species['ML3'] = 10**betas[2]*M*L**3
    species['M(OH)+']  = 10**hydrolysis[metal][0]*M*10**(pH-14)
    species['M(OH)2']  = 10**hydrolysis[metal][1]*M*10**(2*(pH-14))
    return M, L, species

pH = 7.0
M_T, L_T = 1e-3, 5e-3
print(f"Speciation at pH {pH}, [M]_T = {M_T*1e3:g} mM, [L]_T = {L_T*1e3:g} mM\n")
print(f"{'Ligand':<14}{'Metal':<6}{'pM':>7}{'%ML':>8}{'%ML2':>8}{'%ML3':>8}{'%free':>8}{'%OH':>8}")

results = {}
for lig in ligands:
    for met in ['Cu', 'Ni', 'Co']:
        M, L, sp = speciate(M_T, L_T, pH, lig, met)
        pM = -np.log10(M)
        pct = {k: 100*v/M_T for k, v in sp.items()}
        print(f"{lig:<14}{met:<6}{pM:>7.2f}{pct['ML']:>8.1f}{pct.get('ML2',0):>8.1f}"
              f"{pct.get('ML3',0):>8.1f}{pct['M2+']:>8.2f}{pct['M(OH)+']+pct['M(OH)2']:>8.2f}")
        results.setdefault(lig, {})[met] = pM
    print()

print(f"{'Ligand':<14}{'Cu-Co':>8}{'Cu-Ni':>8}{'Ni-Co':>8}{'range':>8}")

          f"{r['Ni']-r['Co']:>8.2f}{max(r.values())-min(r.values()):>8.2f}")

# Also survey pH 6 and 8 for the winner
print("\n\npH sensitivity of L-Histidine:")
print(f"{'pH':<5}{'pCu':>7}{'pNi':>7}{'pCo':>7}{'range':>8}")
for pH in [6.0, 6.5, 7.0, 7.5, 8.0]:
    row = {}
    for met in ['Cu','Ni','Co']:
        M,_,_ = speciate(M_T, L_T, pH, 'L-Histidine', met)
        row[met] = -np.log10(M)
    print(f"{pH:<5}{row['Cu']:>7.2f}{row['Ni']:>7.2f}{row['Co']:>7.2f}"
          f"{max(row.values())-min(row.values()):>8.2f}")

from scipy.optimize import brentq

# =============================================================
# Irving-Williams test: compute 1:1 M(II)/L speciation
# Conditions: 1 mM M(II), 10 mM L, pH 7.00, 25 C, I = 0.1 m
# =============================================================

pH = 7.00
H  = 10**(-pH)
CM = 1.0e-3
CL = 1.0e-2

# ---------- Ligand protonation (log K, I=0.1, 25 C) ----------
# Glycine: pKa1 (COOH)=2.35, pKa2(NH3+)=9.78
# en:      pKa1 = 7.08, pKa2 = 9.89
ligands = {
    "glycine": {
        "pKa": [2.35, 9.78],          # [H2L+/HL, HL/L-]
        "logK": {  # stepwise log K_n
            "Co": [4.64, 3.82],
            "Ni": [5.78, 4.80, 3.40],
            "Cu": [8.15, 6.88],       # no significant ML3
            "Zn": [4.96, 4.24, 2.90],
        }
    },
    "ethylenediamine": {
        "pKa": [7.08, 9.89],          # [H2L2+/HL+, HL+/L]
        "logK": {
            "Co": [5.89, 4.83, 3.10],
            "Ni": [7.35, 6.20, 4.55],
            "Cu": [10.55, 9.05],      # ML3 essentially not formed (Jahn-Teller)
            "Zn": [5.71, 5.16, 1.86],
        }
    },
}

def alpha_L(pKa_list, H):
    """Fraction of ligand in the fully deprotonated form L at [H+]=H."""
    Ka = [10**(-p) for p in pKa_list]         # Ka1 (most acidic) first
    # denom = 1 + H/Ka2 + H^2/(Ka1*Ka2)  (for diprotic)
    denom = 1.0 + H/Ka[1] + H*H/(Ka[0]*Ka[1])
    return 1.0/denom

def solve(logK, CM, CL, alpha):
    """Given stepwise log K_n, total metal CM, total ligand CL, and
    alpha = [L]/CL_free_ligand, solve for [M2+] and [L]."""
    K = [10**k for k in logK]
    beta = np.cumprod(K)                       # beta_n
    N = len(beta)
    # Solve for free [L] by mass balance.
    # Free non-metal-bound ligand = [L]/alpha (all protonation forms)
    # Metal-bound ligand = CM * sum(n*beta_n*[L]^n) / (1 + sum(beta_n*[L]^n))
    def f(L):
        num = sum(n*beta[n-1]*L**n for n in range(1, N+1))
        den = 1.0 + sum(beta[n-1]*L**n for n in range(1, N+1))
        return L/alpha + CM*num/den - CL
    # Free L must lie between essentially 0 and alpha*CL
    Lo, Hi = 1e-25, alpha*CL*1.0
    # Guarantee sign change
    while f(Hi) < 0 and Hi < 1.0:
        Hi *= 10
    L = brentq(f, Lo, Hi, xtol=1e-30, rtol=1e-12)
    den = 1.0 + sum(beta[n-1]*L**n for n in range(1, N+1))
    M   = CM/den
    frac_free = M/CM
    return M, L, frac_free, beta

print(f"pH = {pH:.2f}, CM = {CM*1e3:.1f} mM, CL = {CL*1e3:.1f} mM, I = 0.1 m, 25 C\n")

results = {}
for lname, ldata in ligands.items():
    a = alpha_L(ldata["pKa"], H)
    print(f"=== Ligand: {lname}   pKa = {ldata['pKa']}   alpha(L) at pH7 = {a:.3e} ===")

    results[lname] = {}
    for M, logK in ldata["logK"].items():

        betas = "/".join(f"{np.log10(b):.2f}" for b in beta)

    # Ranking
    order = sorted(results[lname].keys(), key=lambda m: results[lname][m][0])
    print(f"  Suppression ranking (most-suppressed [M2+] first): {' < '.join(order)}\n")

import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import brentq

# Constants at 25 C
Ka = 1.75e-5          # acetic acid
pKa = -np.log10(Ka)
Kw = 1.0e-14

# Setup: titrate 50 mL of 0.010 M HAc with 0.100 M NaOH
V0   = 50.0e-3        # L
CA0  = 0.010          # M  (analytical acetate)
CB0  = 0.100          # M  (NaOH)
n_HA = V0 * CA0
Veq  = n_HA / CB0     # L  -> 5.00 mL

def pH_at(V):
    """Solve exact proton condition for volume V (L) of titrant added."""
    Vt  = V0 + V
    CA  = CA0 * V0 / Vt
    CB  = CB0 * V  / Vt
    # charge balance: CB + [H+] = CA*Ka/(Ka+[H+]) + Kw/[H+]
    f = lambda H: CB + H - CA*Ka/(Ka+H) - Kw/H
    H = brentq(f, 1e-14, 1.0)
    return -np.log10(H)

# --- Curve ---
Vs = np.concatenate([
    np.linspace(0, 0.9*Veq, 40),
    np.linspace(0.9*Veq, 1.1*Veq, 60),   # dense near equivalence
    np.linspace(1.1*Veq, 3.0*Veq, 40),
])
phs = np.array([pH_at(V) for V in Vs])
frac = Vs / Veq                          # equivalents of base added

# --- Key points ---
pH_init = pH_at(0.0)
pH_half = pH_at(0.5*Veq)                 # = pKa (buffer center)
pH_eq   = pH_at(Veq)
pH_2eq  = pH_at(2.0*Veq)

# Buffer region: pH within pKa +/- 1 -> fraction titrated
def frac_at_pH(target):
    g = lambda V: pH_at(V) - target
    return brentq(g, 1e-9, 3*Veq) / Veq
f_lo = frac_at_pH(pKa - 1)
f_hi = frac_at_pH(pKa + 1)

print(f"pKa            = {pKa:.3f}")
print(f"V_equivalence  = {Veq*1e3:.3f} mL")
print(f"pH initial     = {pH_init:.2f}")
print(f"pH at half-eq  = {pH_half:.2f}  (= pKa)")
print(f"pH equivalence = {pH_eq:.2f}")
print(f"pH at 2xVeq    = {pH_2eq:.2f}")
print(f"Buffer window  = pH {pKa-1:.2f} - {pKa+1:.2f}")
print(f"  fraction f   = {f_lo:.3f} - {f_hi:.3f}  (equivalents of NaOH)")

# Sampled values across the pH 2-12 window for the table
targets = [3.4, 3.76, 4.0, 4.5, 4.76, 5.0, 5.5, 5.76, 6.5, 7.0, 8.0, 8.36, 9.0, 10.0, 11.0, 12.0]
print("\n pH     f = V/Veq")
for t in targets:
    try:
        f = frac_at_pH(t)
        print(f" {t:5.2f}   {f:7.4f}")
    except ValueError:
        print(f" {t:5.2f}   (out of range)")

# Save curve for plotting
np.savez('/tmp/curve.npz', frac=frac, ph=phs)

KH2 = 10**logKH2

# Cu(II)-glycinate cumulative formation constants (Gly- as ligand)
logb1 = 8.16    # Cu2+ + Gly-  = CuGly+
logb2 = 15.04   # Cu2+ + 2Gly- = Cu(Gly)2
logb3 = 16.2    # Cu2+ + 3Gly- = Cu(Gly)3-   (minor)
b1, b2, b3 = 10**logb1, 10**logb2, 10**logb3

# Cu hydrolysis (Cu2+ + n OH- = Cu(OH)n^(2-n))
logK_CuOH  = 6.3    # Cu2+ + OH-  = CuOH+
logK_CuOH2 = 11.8   # Cu2+ + 2OH- = Cu(OH)2(aq)
logK_CuOH3 = 14.5   # Cu2+ + 3OH- = Cu(OH)3-
logK_CuOH4 = 16.4   # Cu2+ + 4OH- = Cu(OH)4^2-
KCuOH  = 10**logK_CuOH
KCuOH2 = 10**logK_CuOH2
KCuOH3 = 10**logK_CuOH3
KCuOH4 = 10**logK_CuOH4

# Cu(OH)2(s) solubility - check for precipitation
logKsp_CuOH2 = -19.66   # Cu(OH)2(s) = Cu2+ + 2OH-

C_Cu  = 1.0e-3
C_Gly = 1.0e-2

def solve(pH):
    H  = 10**(-pH)
    OH = 10**(-14 + pH)     # Kw = 1e-14 (thermodynamic; close enough at I=0.1)

    # For a given free [Gly-], compute [Cu2+] from Cu mass balance, then
    # compute total Gly to compare with C_Gly. Find Gly- that closes both.
    alpha_H = 1 + KH1*H + KH1*KH2*H*H   # HGly/Gly-, H2Gly+/Gly- protonation sum

    def cu_from_L(L):
        denom = (1 + b1*L + b2*L*L + b3*L**3
                 + KCuOH*OH + KCuOH2*OH**2 + KCuOH3*OH**3 + KCuOH4*OH**4)
        return C_Cu / denom     # = [Cu2+]

    def residual(logL):
        L  = 10**logL
        Cu = cu_from_L(L)
        # bound glycinate (in Cu complexes)
        bound = Cu * (b1*L + 2*b2*L*L + 3*b3*L**3)
        free  = L * alpha_H
        return free + bound - C_Gly

    logL = brentq(residual, -14, 0)
    L    = 10**logL
    Cu   = cu_from_L(L)

    species = {
        'Cu2+':       Cu,
        'CuGly+':     Cu*b1*L,
        'Cu(Gly)2':   Cu*b2*L*L,
        'Cu(Gly)3-':  Cu*b3*L**3,
        'CuOH+':      Cu*KCuOH*OH,
        'Cu(OH)2(aq)':Cu*KCuOH2*OH**2,
        'Cu(OH)3-':   Cu*KCuOH3*OH**3,
        'Cu(OH)4^2-': Cu*KCuOH4*OH**4,
    }
    # saturation w.r.t. Cu(OH)2(s)
    SI = np.log10(Cu*OH**2) - logKsp_CuOH2
    return L, species, SI

pH_grid = np.arange(2.0, 12.01, 0.1)
frac = {k: [] for k in ['Cu2+','CuGly+','Cu(Gly)2','Cu(Gly)3-',
                        'CuOH+','Cu(OH)2(aq)','Cu(OH)3-','Cu(OH)4^2-']}
SI_list = []
for pH in pH_grid:
    _, sp, SI = solve(pH)
    for k in frac:
        frac[k].append(100*sp[k]/C_Cu)
    SI_list.append(SI)

                            logK_FeIII_L_OH, logK_FeII_L, logK_FeII_HL,

# Cu / Cu-ammine / H2O Pourbaix diagram

# (Smith & Martell / Baes & Mesmer tabulation)

# NH4+  = NH3 + H+     pKa = 9.24
pKa_NH4 = 9.24

import numpy as np

# ================ EQUILIBRIUM CONSTANTS ================
# Fe(III) hydrolysis (log *β_n: Fe³⁺ + n H₂O ⇌ Fe(OH)_n^(3-n) + n H⁺)
log_beta_hyd = [-2.19, -5.67, -13.6, -21.6]

log_Ks0_Fe_OH3 = 3.5

# EDTA (Y⁴⁻) - pKa values and complex constants (I=0.1, 25°C)

log_K_FeY      = 25.1   # Fe³⁺ + Y⁴⁻ → FeY⁻
log_K_FeOHY_OH = 6.45   # FeY⁻ + OH⁻ → FeOHY²⁻

# Citrate (Cit³⁻) - pKa values and complex constants
pKa_cit = [3.13, 4.76, 6.40]
log_K_FeCit         = 11.85  # Fe³⁺ + Cit³⁻ → FeCit(aq)
log_beta_FeCit2     = 15.5   # Fe³⁺ + 2Cit³⁻ → Fe(Cit)₂³⁻
log_K_FeOHCit_OH    = 4.2    # FeCit + OH⁻ → FeOHCit⁻
log_K_FeOH2Cit_OH   = 3.7    # FeOHCit⁻ + OH⁻ → Fe(OH)₂Cit²⁻
# Polynuclear trimer (Königsberger, Silva et al.):
# 3Fe³⁺ + 3Cit³⁻ ⇌ Fe₃(OH)(Cit)₃⁴⁻ + H⁺
log_beta_Fe3_tri = 49.0

Kw = 1e-14
Fe_tot = 1e-3   # 1 mM total Fe
L_tot  = 5e-3   # 5 mM total ligand

def alpha_free(H, pKa_list):
    """Fraction of ligand in fully deprotonated form."""
    n = len(pKa_list)
    Ka = [10**(-p) for p in pKa_list]
    denom = 1.0
    for i in range(n):
        prod = 1.0
        for j in range(i+1):
            prod *= Ka[n-1-j]
        denom += (H**(i+1)) / prod
    return 1.0/denom

def analyze(pH, ligand):
    H = 10**(-pH); OH = Kw/H
    Fe3_sat = 10**log_Ks0_Fe_OH3 * H**3
    # Soluble hydrolysis species (in equilibrium with solid)
    Fe_hyd = Fe3_sat*(1 + 10**log_beta_hyd[0]/H + 10**log_beta_hyd[1]/H**2
                      + 10**log_beta_hyd[2]/H**3 + 10**log_beta_hyd[3]/H**4)
    if ligand=='EDTA':
        aL = alpha_free(H, pKa_edta)
        L_free = aL*(L_tot - Fe_tot)
        mod = 1 + 10**log_K_FeOHY_OH * OH
        Fe_L_max = 10**log_K_FeY * Fe3_sat * L_free * mod
    else:  # citrate
        aL = alpha_free(H, pKa_cit)
        L_free = aL*(L_tot - Fe_tot)
        K1 = 10**log_K_FeCit
        Kb2 = 10**(log_beta_FeCit2 - log_K_FeCit)
        Ka = 10**log_K_FeOHCit_OH
        Kb = 10**log_K_FeOH2Cit_OH

        Fe_mono = K1*Fe3_sat*L_free*mod
        Fe_tri  = 3*10**log_beta_Fe3_tri * Fe3_sat**3 * L_free**3 / H
        Fe_L_max = Fe_mono + Fe_tri
    return min((Fe_L_max + Fe_hyd)/Fe_tot, 1.0)

description: Compute Cu(II) speciation vs pH for EDTA and NTA systems using iterative mass-balance solver.
command:
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/cu_speciation.py
import numpy as np

# ---- Constants (25 C, I = 0.1 M; Martell & Smith / NIST 46) ----

# EDTA: stepwise protonation of Y^4- (log K)
logK_EDTA_prot = [10.19, 6.13, 2.69, 2.00]  # K1..K4

# Cu-EDTA
logK_CuY   = 18.78   # Cu2+ + Y4- -> CuY2-
logK_CuHY  = 3.00    # CuY2- + H+ -> CuHY-  (protonation of complex)
logK_CuOHY = 2.50    # CuY2- + OH- -> Cu(OH)Y3-

# NTA: stepwise protonation of T^3-
logK_NTA_prot = [9.65, 2.52, 1.81]  # K1..K3

# Cu-NTA
logK_CuT   = 12.96   # Cu2+ + T3- -> CuT-
logb2_CuT2 = 17.40   # Cu2+ + 2 T3- -> Cu(T)2^4-
logK_CuHT  = 1.70    # CuT- + H+ -> CuHT

# Cu(II) hydrolysis: Cu2+ + n H2O -> Cu(OH)n + n H+ ; log *beta
logsb_Cu = [-8.0, -16.2, -26.3, -39.6]  # n = 1..4

Kw     = 1e-14
Cu_tot = 1e-3
L_tot  = 5e-3

def inv_alpha_Cu_inorg(pH):
    H = 10**(-pH)
    s = 1.0
    for n, lb in enumerate(logsb_Cu, 1):
        s += 10**lb / H**n
    return s   # (Sum inorganic Cu)/[Cu2+]

def solve_EDTA(pH):
    H, OH = 10**(-pH), Kw/10**(-pH)
    K1,K2,K3,K4 = [10**k for k in logK_EDTA_prot]
    inv_aY = 1 + K1*H + K1*K2*H**2 + K1*K2*K3*H**3 + K1*K2*K3*K4*H**4
    aY = 1/inv_aY
    inv_aCu = inv_alpha_Cu_inorg(pH)
    KCuY   = 10**logK_CuY
    KCuHY  = 10**logK_CuHY
    KCuOHY = 10**logK_CuOHY
    tern   = 1 + KCuHY*H + KCuOHY*OH   # (all CuY-based)/CuY
    # Solve x = [Cu2+], y = [Y4-]
    x = 1e-15; y = aY*(L_tot-Cu_tot)
    for _ in range(500):
        y_n = L_tot / (1/aY + KCuY*x*tern)
        x_n = Cu_tot / (inv_aCu + KCuY*y_n*tern)
        if abs(x_n-x)/max(x,1e-40) < 1e-10: break
        x, y = x_n, y_n
    return x

def solve_NTA(pH):
    H, OH = 10**(-pH), Kw/10**(-pH)
    K1,K2,K3 = [10**k for k in logK_NTA_prot]
    inv_aT = 1 + K1*H + K1*K2*H**2 + K1*K2*K3*H**3
    aT = 1/inv_aT
    inv_aCu = inv_alpha_Cu_inorg(pH)
    KCuT  = 10**logK_CuT
    b2    = 10**logb2_CuT2
    KCuHT = 10**logK_CuHT
    x = 1e-10; y = aT*(L_tot-Cu_tot)
    for _ in range(500):
        # L balance: 2 b2 x y^2 + (1/aT + KCuT*x*(1+KCuHT*H))*y - L_tot = 0
        a = 2*b2*x
        b = 1/aT + KCuT*x*(1 + KCuHT*H)
        c = -L_tot
        y_n = (-b + np.sqrt(b*b - 4*a*c))/(2*a) if a>0 else -c/b
        denom = inv_aCu + KCuT*y_n*(1+KCuHT*H) + b2*y_n**2
        x_n = Cu_tot/denom
        if abs(x_n-x)/max(x,1e-40) < 1e-10: break
        x, y = x_n, y_n
    return x, y, b2*y**2*x, KCuT*y*x  # also return Cu(T)2 and CuT for diagnostics

# --- pH 3..10 scan ---
pH_scan = np.arange(3.0, 10.001, 0.1)
pCu_E, pCu_N = [], []
for pH in pH_scan:
    xE = solve_EDTA(pH)
    xN, _, _, _ = solve_NTA(pH)
    pCu_E.append(-np.log10(xE))
    pCu_N.append(-np.log10(xN))

print(f"{'pH':>5} {'pCu(EDTA)':>10} {'[Cu2+] EDTA':>14} {'pCu(NTA)':>10} {'[Cu2+] NTA':>14}")
for pH in [3.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, 8.0, 9.0, 10.0]:
    xE = solve_EDTA(pH)
    xN, y, cuT2, cuT = solve_NTA(pH)
    frac_CuT2 = cuT2/(cuT2+cuT) if (cuT2+cuT)>0 else 0
    print(f"{pH:5.1f} {-np.log10(xE):10.2f} {xE:14.3e} {-np.log10(xN):10.2f} {xN:14.3e}  (Cu(T)2 frac={frac_CuT2:.2f})")

# --- Low-pH dissociation ---
print("\n-- Fraction of Cu as free Cu2+ at low pH --")
print(f"{'pH':>5} {'EDTA %free':>12} {'NTA %free':>12}")
for pH in [1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0]:
    xE = solve_EDTA(pH)
    xN, _, _, _ = solve_NTA(pH)
    fE = min(xE/Cu_tot, 1.0)*100
    fN = min(xN/Cu_tot, 1.0)*100
    print(f"{pH:5.1f} {fE:12.4f} {fN:12.4f}")

# --- pH where free Cu reaches 1% ---
from scipy.optimize import brentq
def free_frac_EDTA(pH): return solve_EDTA(pH)/Cu_tot - 0.01
def free_frac_NTA(pH):
    x,_,_,_ = solve_NTA(pH); return x/Cu_tot - 0.01
try:
    pH1E = brentq(free_frac_EDTA, 0.5, 4.0)
    print(f"\n1% free Cu²⁺ from EDTA at pH ≈ {pH1E:.2f}")
except Exception as e: print("EDTA 1% root err:", e)
try:
    pH1N = brentq(free_frac_NTA, 0.5, 5.0)
    print(f"1% free Cu²⁺ from NTA  at pH ≈ {pH1N:.2f}")
except Exception as e: print("NTA 1% root err:", e)

# Save the full scan to files for plotting
np.savez('/tmp/pcu_scan.npz', pH=pH_scan, pCu_E=np.array(pCu_E), pCu_N=np.array(pCu_N))
EOF

import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import brentq

# ---------------- constants ----------------
T = 298.15; R = 8.314462618; F = 96485.33212
LN10 = np.log(10.0)
FV = R*T*LN10/F            # 0.059159 V per decade
I = 0.1; A_DH = 0.509
def logg(z):
    s = np.sqrt(I)
    return -A_DH*z*z*(s/(1+s) - 0.3*I)
g1, g2 = logg(1), logg(2)

# ---------------- reference data (activity basis, I=0 unless noted) ----------------
E0_Ni      = -0.237          # Ni2+ + 2e- = Ni   (dfG Ni2+ = -45.7 kJ/mol, NBS/CODATA; Beverskog & Puigdomenech 1997)
logKs0_cr  = 11.0            # beta-Ni(OH)2(cr) + 2H+ = Ni2+ + 2H2O  (crystalline)
logKs0_am  = 12.7            # freshly precipitated Ni(OH)2 (sensitivity case)
logb_h     = [-9.86, -19.0, -30.0, -44.0]   # Ni2+ + nH2O = Ni(OH)n(2-n) + nH+  (Baes & Mesmer)
E0_NiOOH   = 1.32            # beta-NiOOH + H+ + e- = beta-Ni(OH)2   (0.49 V vs SHE at a(OH-)=1, Bode et al.)
# glycine, concentration constants already at I=0.1 M, 25 C (Martell & Smith / IUPAC)
logKH1, logKH2 = 9.57, 2.35
logb_gly = [5.78, 10.58, 14.00]

def build(logKs0=logKs0_cr, E0_Ni=E0_Ni, logb_gly=logb_gly, E0_NiOOH=E0_NiOOH):
    p = {}
    # hydrolysis, concentration basis
    p['bh'] = [10**(logb_h[0] - (g1 + g1 - g2)),
               10**(logb_h[1] - (2*g1 - g2)),
               10**(logb_h[2] - (g1 + 3*g1 - g2)),
               10**(logb_h[3] - (g2 + 4*g1 - g2))]
    p['logKs0c'] = logKs0 - (g2 - 2*g1)
    p['logK_Ni']  = 2*E0_Ni/FV - (-g2)                     # Ni2+ + 2e = Ni
    p['logK_OOH'] = (E0_NiOOH/FV + logKs0) - (g2 - 3*g1)   # NiOOH + 3H+ + e = Ni2+ + 2H2O
    p['KH1'], p['KH2'] = 10**logKH1, 10**logKH2
    p['bg'] = [10**v for v in logb_gly]
    return p

NAMES = ['Ni(s)','Ni2+','NiOH+','Ni(OH)2(aq)','Ni(OH)3-','Ni(OH)4^2-','NiGly+','NiGly2','NiGly3-','Ni(OH)2(s)','NiOOH(s)']

def speciate(pH, p, NiT=1e-3, GlyT=1e-2):
    h = 10.0**(-pH)
    bh = p['bh']; b1,b2,b3 = p['bg']
    Dh = 1 + bh[0]/h + bh[1]/h**2 + bh[2]/h**3 + bh[3]/h**4
    P  = 1 + p['KH1']*h + p['KH1']*p['KH2']*h*h
    def xof(y): return NiT/(Dh + b1*y + b2*y*y + b3*y**3)
    def res(ly):
        y = 10**ly
        return y*P + xof(y)*(b1*y + 2*b2*y*y + 3*b3*y**3) - GlyT
    ly = brentq(res, -25, np.log10(GlyT/P)+1e-12, xtol=1e-13)
    y = 10**ly; x = xof(y)
    conc = np.array([0.0, x, bh[0]*x/h, bh[1]*x/h**2, bh[2]*x/h**3, bh[3]*x/h**4,
                     b1*x*y, b2*x*y*y, b3*x*y**3, 0.0, 0.0])
    return x, y, conc

def solid_logNi(pH, E, p):
    pe = E/FV
    return np.array([-p['logK_Ni'] + 2*pe,            # Ni(s)
                     p['logKs0c'] - 2*pH,             # Ni(OH)2(s)
                     p['logK_OOH'] - 3*pH - pe])      # NiOOH(s)
SOLID_IDX = [0, 9, 10]

def label_grid(pHs, Es, p, NiT=1e-3, GlyT=1e-2):
    logx = np.empty(len(pHs)); aqlab = np.empty(len(pHs), dtype=int); fr = np.empty((len(pHs), 11))
    for i, pH in enumerate(pHs):
        x, y, c = speciate(pH, p, NiT, GlyT)
        logx[i] = np.log10(x); aqlab[i] = int(np.argmax(c)); fr[i] = c/NiT
    lab = np.empty((len(Es), len(pHs)), dtype=int)
    pe = Es/FV
    for i, pH in enumerate(pHs):
        s = np.vstack([-p['logK_Ni'] + 2*pe, np.full_like(pe, p['logKs0c'] - 2*pH), p['logK_OOH'] - 3*pH - pe])
        j = np.argmin(s, axis=0); smin = s[j, np.arange(len(pe))]
        col = np.where(smin < logx[i], np.array(SOLID_IDX)[j], aqlab[i])
        lab[:, i] = col
    return lab, logx, aqlab, fr

if __name__ == '__main__':
    p = build()
    print('FV=%.5f  logg1=%.3f logg2=%.3f' % (FV, g1, g2))
    print('logKs0c=%.3f logK_Ni=%.3f (E0\'=%.4f V) logK_OOH=%.3f' % (p['logKs0c'], p['logK_Ni'], p['logK_Ni']*FV/2, p['logK_OOH']))
    for pH in [2,4,5,5.5,5.8,6,6.5,7,7.5,8,8.5,9,9.5,10,10.5,11,11.3,11.5,12,13,14]:
        x,y,c = speciate(pH,p)
        f = c/1e-3
        top = np.argsort(f)[::-1][:3]
        sN = solid_logNi(pH, 0.0, p)
        E_Ni = (np.log10(x) + p['logK_Ni'])*FV/2
        E_OOH = (p['logK_OOH'] - 3*pH - np.log10(x))*FV
        ppt = 'PPT' if p['logKs0c']-2*pH < np.log10(x) else ''
        print('pH %5.2f  [Gly-]=%.2e  log[Ni2+]=%6.2f  %s  E(Ni/NiII)=%6.3f  E(NiII/NiOOH)=%6.3f  %s' % (pH, y, np.log10(x),
              ', '.join('%s %.1f%%' % (NAMES[k], 100*f[k]) for k in top), E_Ni, E_OOH, ppt))

import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from model import *

def crossings(p, NiT=1e-3, GlyT=1e-2):
    out = {}
    def frac(pH, k):
        x,y,c = speciate(pH,p,NiT,GlyT); return c/NiT
    # aqueous crossovers
    out['Ni2+/NiGly+']  = brentq(lambda s: frac(s,1)[1]-frac(s,1)[6], 3, 8)
    out['NiGly+/NiGly2']= brentq(lambda s: frac(s,1)[6]-frac(s,1)[7], 5, 9)
    out['NiGly2/NiGly3-']=brentq(lambda s: frac(s,1)[7]-frac(s,1)[8], 6, 11)
    # precipitation onset of Ni(OH)2(s)
    out['ppt Ni(OH)2']  = brentq(lambda s: (p['logKs0c']-2*s) - np.log10(speciate(s,p,NiT,GlyT)[0]), 6, 14)
    # max fraction of each complex
    pHs = np.linspace(0,14,1401)
    fr = np.array([speciate(s,p,NiT,GlyT)[2]/NiT for s in pHs])
    for k in [6,7,8]:
        i = np.argmax(fr[:,k]); out['max '+NAMES[k]] = (pHs[i], fr[i,k])
    return out, pHs, fr

p = build()
out, pHs, fr = crossings(p)
for k,v in out.items(): print(k, v)

def Eline(pH, p, NiT=1e-3, GlyT=1e-2):
    x = speciate(pH,p,NiT,GlyT)[0]
    E_Ni  = (np.log10(x) + p['logK_Ni'])*FV/2
    E_OOH = (p['logK_OOH'] - 3*pH - np.log10(x))*FV
    # solid-solid lines
    lNi_s = p['logKs0c'] - 2*pH
    E_Ni_s  = (lNi_s + p['logK_Ni'])*FV/2
    E_OOH_s = (p['logK_OOH'] - 3*pH - lNi_s)*FV
    return E_Ni, E_OOH, E_Ni_s, E_OOH_s
print('\npH   E(Ni/Ni(II)aq)  E(Ni(II)aq/NiOOH)  E(Ni/Ni(OH)2s)  E(Ni(OH)2s/NiOOH)  H2 line  O2 line')
for pH in [0,2,4,5.79,7,8,8.23,9,9.57,10,10.86,11,12,13,14]:
    a,b,c,d = Eline(pH,p)
    print('%5.2f  %8.3f  %8.3f  %8.3f  %8.3f  %8.3f %8.3f' % (pH,a,b,c,d, -0.0063-FV*pH, 1.2227-FV*pH))

print('\n--- sensitivity ---')
for label, kw in [('fresh Ni(OH)2 logKs0=12.7', dict(logKs0=12.7)),
                  ('E0(Ni)=-0.257', dict(E0_Ni=-0.257)),
                  ('gly betas -0.1', dict(logb_gly=[5.68,10.48,13.90])),
                  ('gly betas +0.1', dict(logb_gly=[5.88,10.68,14.10])),
                  ('NiOOH E0 1.39', dict(E0_NiOOH=1.39))]:
    pp = build(**kw); o,_,_ = crossings(pp)
    a = Eline(10.0, pp)
    print(label, {k:(round(v,2) if not isinstance(v,tuple) else (round(v[0],2), round(v[1],3))) for k,v in o.items()}, 'E lines @pH10:', [round(t,3) for t in a])

import numpy as np, json
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from skimage import measure
from model import *

p = build()
NiT, GlyT = 1e-3, 1e-2
pHs = np.round(np.arange(0, 14.0001, 0.01), 4)
Es  = np.round(np.arange(-1.0, 2.0001, 0.005), 4)
lab, logx, aqlab, fr_hyp = label_grid(pHs, Es, p, NiT, GlyT)

# ---- plot geometry ----
L, Rt, Tp, B = 64, 820, 24, 548
W, H = Rt-L, B-Tp
def X(pH): return L + pH/14*W
def Y(E):  return B - (E+1.0)/3.0*H

polys = {}   # label -> list of point lists (svg coords)
for k in np.unique(lab):
    m = np.pad((lab==k).astype(float), 1)
    cs = measure.find_contours(m, 0.5)
    out = []
    for c in cs:
        r = np.clip(c[:,0]-1, 0, len(Es)-1); q = np.clip(c[:,1]-1, 0, len(pHs)-1)
        E = -1.0 + r*0.005; pH = q*0.01
        pts = np.column_stack([X(pH), Y(E)])
        pts = measure.approximate_polygon(pts, tolerance=0.5)
        if len(pts) >= 3: out.append(pts)
    polys[int(k)] = out

def path_d(pts):
    return 'M' + ' L'.join('%.1f %.1f' % (x,y) for x,y in pts) + ' Z'

# largest-region centroids (for label placement hints)
cent = {}
for k, ps in polys.items():
    best = max(ps, key=lambda q: abs(0.5*np.sum(q[:,0]*np.roll(q[:,1],-1) - np.roll(q[:,0],-1)*q[:,1])))
    cent[k] = (float(best[:,0].mean()), float(best[:,1].mean()), len(ps), len(best))
for k,v in cent.items(): print(NAMES[k], 'centroid svg=(%.0f,%.0f)  pieces=%d pts=%d' % v)

# ---- actual (with-solid) distribution vs pH within the Ni(II) domain ----
def dist_actual(pH):
    x, y, c = speciate(pH, p, NiT, GlyT)
    lsat = p['logKs0c'] - 2*pH
    if lsat < np.log10(x):   # solid present: fix x at solubility, re-solve y
        x = 10**lsat; h = 10**(-pH); bh = p['bh']; b1,b2,b3 = p['bg']
        P = 1 + p['KH1']*h + p['KH1']*p['KH2']*h*h
        f = lambda ly: (10**ly)*P + x*(b1*10**ly + 2*b2*10**(2*ly) + 3*b3*10**(3*ly)) - GlyT
        y = 10**brentq(f, -25, np.log10(GlyT/P)+1e-12)
        c = np.array([0, x, bh[0]*x/h, bh[1]*x/h**2, bh[2]*x/h**3, bh[3]*x/h**4, b1*x*y, b2*x*y*y, b3*x*y**3, 0, 0])
        c[9] = NiT - c.sum()
    return c/NiT, np.log10(x)

pH_c = np.round(np.arange(0, 14.0001, 0.05), 3)
FR = np.array([dist_actual(s)[0] for s in pH_c])
LOGX = np.array([np.log10(speciate(s,p,NiT,GlyT)[0]) for s in pH_c])   # hypothetical free Ni2+ (drives solid tests)
AQ  = np.array([int(np.argmax(speciate(s,p,NiT,GlyT)[2])) for s in pH_c])

# distribution panel geometry
dL, dR, dT, dB = 64, 820, 20, 200
def dX(pH): return dL + pH/14*(dR-dL)
def dY(f):  return dB - f*(dB-dT)
curves = {}
for k in [1,6,7,8,9,2,3,4,5]:
    pts = np.column_stack([dX(pH_c), dY(FR[:,k])])
    pts = measure.approximate_polygon(pts, tolerance=0.3)
    curves[k] = 'M' + ' L'.join('%.1f %.1f' % (x,y) for x,y in pts)

data = dict(
    polys={k:[path_d(q) for q in ps] for k,ps in polys.items()},
    curves=curves,
    pH=pH_c.tolist(),
    fr=np.round(FR,4).tolist(),
    logx=np.round(LOGX,3).tolist(),
    aq=AQ.tolist(),
    consts=dict(FV=FV, logK_Ni=p['logK_Ni'], logKs0c=p['logKs0c'], logK_OOH=p['logK_OOH'],
                logKs0c_fresh=build(logKs0=12.7)['logKs0c']),
    geom=dict(L=L,R=Rt,T=Tp,B=B,dL=dL,dR=dR,dT=dT,dB=dB),
)
json.dump(data, open('geom.json','w'))
print('json size', len(json.dumps(data))//1024, 'kB')

nE,nP=lab.shape[1:]
dp, dE = 0.05, 0.01
def boundaries(L):
    pts=collections.defaultdict(list)
    # horizontal neighbours (pH direction)
    a=L[:,:-1]; b=L[:,1:]
    ii,jj=np.where(a!=b)
    for i,j in zip(ii,jj):
        key=tuple(sorted((int(a[i,j]),int(b[i,j]))))
        pts[key].append((pHs[j]+dp/2, Es[i]))
    a=L[:-1,:]; b=L[1:,:]
    ii,jj=np.where(a!=b)
    for i,j in zip(ii,jj):
        key=tuple(sorted((int(a[i,j]),int(b[i,j]))))
        pts[key].append((pHs[j], Es[i]+dE/2))
    return pts
def junctions(L):
    out=[]
    for i in range(nE-1):
        for j in range(nP-1):
            s=set([int(L[i,j]),int(L[i,j+1]),int(L[i+1,j]),int(L[i+1,j+1])])
            if len(s)>=3: out.append((tuple(sorted(s)), pHs[j]+dp/2, Es[i]+dE/2))
    # cluster by label set and proximity
    clusters=[]
    for key,p,e in out:
        for c in clusters:
            if c['key']==key and abs(c['pH']-p)<0.4 and abs(c['E']-e)<0.08:
                c['pts'].append((p,e)); c['pH']=np.mean([q[0] for q in c['pts']]); c['E']=np.mean([q[1] for q in c['pts']]); break
        else:
            clusters.append(dict(key=key,pH=p,E=e,pts=[(p,e)]))
    return clusters
report={}
for j,met in enumerate(['Cu','Fe']):
    L=lab[j]
    B=boundaries(L)
    rows=[]
    for key,p in sorted(B.items(), key=lambda kv:-len(kv[1])):
        p=np.array(p); n=len(p)
        if n<6: continue
        pr=(p[:,0].min(),p[:,0].max()); er=(p[:,1].min(),p[:,1].max())
        kind=''; eq=''
        if pr[1]-pr[0] < 0.12:
            kind='acid-base (vertical)'; eq=f"pH = {p[:,0].mean():.2f}"
        elif er[1]-er[0] < 0.015:
            kind='redox (horizontal)'; eq=f"E = {p[:,1].mean():+.3f} V"
        else:
            # fit E = a + b pH
            A=np.vstack([np.ones(n),p[:,0]]).T
            (a,b),res,_,_=np.linalg.lstsq(A,p[:,1],rcond=None)
            rms=np.sqrt(np.mean((A@[a,b]-p[:,1])**2))
            kind='redox (sloping)'; eq=f"E = {a:+.3f} {b:+.4f}·pH  (rms {rms*1000:.0f} mV)"
            if rms>0.012: kind='redox (curved)'
        # sample points at 5 pH values
        samp=[]
        for q in np.linspace(pr[0],pr[1],5):
            k=np.argmin(np.abs(p[:,0]-q)); samp.append((round(float(p[k,0]),2),round(float(p[k,1]),3)))
        rows.append(dict(a=names[key[0]],b=names[key[1]],n=int(n),pH=[round(float(x),2) for x in pr],E=[round(float(x),3) for x in er],kind=kind,eq=eq,samples=samp))
    J=junctions(L)
    jr=[dict(species=[names[k] for k in c['key']],pH=round(float(c['pH']),2),E=round(float(c['E']),3),n=len(c['pts'])) for c in J]
    report[met]=dict(boundaries=rows,junctions=jr)
    print('=====',met,'boundaries (>=6 pts):')
    for r in rows: print(f"  {r['a']:24s} | {r['b']:24s} n={r['n']:4d} pH {r['pH']} E {r['E']} {r['kind']:22s} {r['eq']}")
    print('  junctions:')
    for r in jr: print('   ',r)
# joint crossings: junctions of the joint label
JL = lab[0].astype(np.int64)*1000 + lab[1].astype(np.int64)
Jj = junctions(JL)
cross=[]
cuJ=set((round(c['pH'],1),round(c['E'],2)) for c in report['Cu']['junctions']); 
for c in Jj:
    cu=set(k//1000 for k in c['key']); fe=set(k%1000 for k in c['key'])

report['crossings']=cross

json.dump(report, open('report.json','w'), indent=1)

description: Run Fe(III)/EDTA/citrate speciation model over pH 4-14
command:
mkdir -p /home/claude && cat > /home/claude/fe_spec.py << 'EOF'
import numpy as np

# ---- Davies at I=0.1, 25 C: log g(z) = -0.107 z^2 ; used only to move I=0 constants to I=0.1
def lg(z): return -0.1069*z*z

# Species: (p Fe, q L, r H, logbeta at I=0.1, name)
# Fe hydrolysis: Baes&Mesmer / MINTEQ I=0 values corrected to I=0.1
hyd = [
 (1,0,-1, -2.19 + lg(3)-lg(2)-lg(1),  'FeOH2+'),
 (1,0,-2, -5.67 + lg(3)-lg(1)-2*lg(1),'Fe(OH)2+'),
 (1,0,-3,-12.56 + lg(3)-3*lg(1),       'Fe(OH)3(aq)'),
 (1,0,-4,-21.60 + lg(3)-lg(1)-4*lg(1), 'Fe(OH)4-'),
 (2,0,-2, -2.95 + 2*lg(3)-lg(4)-2*lg(1),'Fe2(OH)2 4+'),
 (3,0,-4, -6.30 + 3*lg(3)-lg(5)-4*lg(1),'Fe3(OH)4 5+'),
]
# EDTA (Y4-), NIST I=0.1
pk_edta=[10.17,6.11,2.68,2.0,1.5,0.0]
edta = [(0,1,i+1, sum(pk_edta[:i+1]), f'H{i+1}Y') for i in range(6)]
edta += [
 (1,1, 0, 25.1,            'FeY-'),
 (1,1, 1, 25.1+1.4,        'FeHY'),
 (1,1,-1, 25.1-7.49,       'Fe(OH)Y2-'),
 (1,1,-2, 25.1-7.49-9.4,   'Fe(OH)2Y3-'),
 (2,2,-2, 2*(25.1-7.49)+1.6,'(FeY)2O4-'),
]
# Citrate (Cit3-), NIST I=0.1 protonation; Fe-citrate from Vukosav 2012 (L4- basis) converted with alcohol pKa 14.4 (Silva 2009)
pk_cit=[5.69,4.35,2.87]
cit = [(0,1,i+1, sum(pk_cit[:i+1]), f'H{i+1}Cit') for i in range(3)]
cit += [
 (1,1, 1, 12.2,          'FeHCit+'),
 (1,1, 0, 25.69-14.4,    'FeCit'),
 (1,1,-1, 25.69-14.4-2.7,'Fe(H-1Cit)-'),
 (1,2, 0, 48.06-28.8,    'Fe(Cit)2 3-'),
 (1,2,-1, 44.60-28.8,    'Fe(Cit)(H-1Cit)4-'),
 (1,2,-2, 38.85-28.8,    'Fe(H-1Cit)2 5-'),
]
solids = {'Fe(OH)3(am,fresh) log*Ksp0=4.89': 4.89 + 3*lg(1)-lg(3),
          'ferrihydrite(aged) log*Ksp0=3.2':  3.2  + 3*lg(1)-lg(3),
          'goethite log*Ksp0=-1.0':          -1.0  + 3*lg(1)-lg(3)}

def conc(sp, lFe, lL, pH):
    return [(p,q,10**(lb + p*lFe + q*lL - r*pH), nm) for (p,q,r,lb,nm) in sp]

def solve(sp, FeT, LT, pH, lFe_fixed=None):
    def fe_of_L(lL):
        if lFe_fixed is not None: return lFe_fixed
        lo,hi=-40.0,0.0
        for _ in range(200):
            mid=0.5*(lo+hi)
            s=sum(p*c for p,q,c,nm in conc(sp,mid,lL,pH))
            lo,hi=(mid,hi) if s<FeT else (lo,mid)
        return 0.5*(lo+hi)
    lo,hi=-40.0,np.log10(LT)
    for _ in range(200):
        mid=0.5*(lo+hi)
        lFe=fe_of_L(mid)
        s=sum(q*c for p,q,c,nm in conc(sp,lFe,mid,pH))
        lo,hi=(mid,hi) if s<LT else (lo,mid)
    lL=0.5*(lo+hi); lFe=fe_of_L(lL)
    return lFe,lL,conc(sp,lFe,lL,pH)

FeT,LT=1e-3,5e-3
systems={'EDTA':hyd+edta,'citrate':hyd+cit}
pHs=np.round(np.arange(4,14.01,0.25),2)
res={}
for name,sp in systems.items():
    rows=[]
    for pH in pHs:
        lFe,lL,cs=solve(sp,FeT,LT,pH)
        rows.append((pH,-lFe,cs))
    res[name]=rows

print("pFe (-log[Fe3+]) buffered by ligand, and solubility lines (pFe_sat = 3pH - log*Ksp_c):")
print("pH   EDTA   cit  | am-fresh  ferri-aged  goethite")
for i,pH in enumerate(pHs):
    if pH<=9.0 or pH%1==0:
        line=f"{pH:4.2f} {res['EDTA'][i][1]:6.2f} {res['citrate'][i][1]:6.2f} |"
        for k,v in solids.items(): line+=f" {3*pH-v:8.2f}"
        print(line)

print("\nFirst pH at which each solid becomes supersaturated (SI>0), scanning 4-14:")
for name in systems:
    for k,v in solids.items():
        cross=None
        for i in range(len(pHs)-1):
            si0=(3*pHs[i]-v)-res[name][i][1]   # SI = pFe_sat - pFe  (>0 => supersaturated)
            si1=(3*pHs[i+1]-v)-res[name][i+1][1]
            if si0<=0<si1:
                cross=pHs[i]+0.25*(-si0)/(si1-si0); break
            if si0>0 and i==0: cross=pHs[0]; break
        print(f"  {name:8s} vs {k:38s}: {'never (<=14)' if cross is None else f'pH {cross:.2f}'}")

print("\nSpeciation (% of total Fe), no solid allowed:")
for name in systems:
    print(f"--- {name}")
    for pH in [4,5,6,7,8,9]:
        i=list(pHs).index(pH)
        cs=res[name][i][2]
        fe=[(p*c/FeT*100,nm) for p,q,c,nm in cs if p>0]
        fe.sort(reverse=True)
        print(f"pH {pH}: "+", ".join(f"{nm} {x:.1f}%" for x,nm in fe if x>0.3))

print("\nSI (log) vs fresh Fe(OH)3(am) at pH 9:")
v=solids['Fe(OH)3(am,fresh) log*Ksp0=4.89']
i=list(pHs).index(9.0)
for name in systems: print(f"  {name}: SI = {(3*9-v)-res[name][i][1]:.2f}")

# Dissolved Fe if solid (fresh am) forced present, for citrate at pH 9-12
print("\nDissolved Fe (mM) in equilibrium with fresh Fe(OH)3(am), where supersaturated:")
for name,sp in systems.items():
    for pH in [9,10,11,12]:
        lFe=v-3*pH
        lFe2,lL,cs=solve(sp,FeT,LT,pH,lFe_fixed=lFe)
        diss=sum(p*c for p,q,c,nm in cs)
        print(f"  {name} pH {pH}: dissolved {min(diss,FeT)*1e3:.3f} mM  ({'undersat, all dissolved' if diss>=FeT else 'solid present'})")
EOF

import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

# ---- constants, 25 C, I = 0.1 m (NIST 46 / Baes & Mesmer / Pourbaix) ----
NT, GT = 1e-3, 1e-2
pKa1, pKa2 = 2.35, 9.57                # H2Gly+ / HGly / Gly-
lb = {1:5.78, 2:10.58, 3:14.0}          # Ni + nGly- -> NiGly_n
lKOH = -9.86                            # Ni2+ + H2O -> NiOH+ + H+
lKs  = 12.7                             # Ni(OH)2(s) + 2H+ -> Ni2+ + 2H2O (fresh)
lK3  = -30.0                            # Ni2+ + 3H2O -> Ni(OH)3- + 3H+
E0_Ni = -0.257                          # Ni2+/Ni
E0_NiOOH = 1.319 + 0.05916*lKs          # NiOOH + 3H+ + e -> Ni2+ + 2H2O (from 0.49 V vs SHE at pH14)
b = {n:10**v for n,v in lb.items()}; KOH=10**lKOH; Ks=10**lKs; K3=10**lK3
Ka1,Ka2 = 10**-pKa1, 10**-pKa2

def side(m,h):        # Ni(II) side-reaction coeff excluding glycine
    return 1 + KOH/h + K3/h**3
def gly_balance(lg,m,h):
    g=10**lg; ag = 1 + h/Ka2 + h*h/(Ka1*Ka2)
    return g*ag + m*(b[1]*g+2*b[2]*g**2+3*b[3]*g**3) - GT
def ni_diss(m,g,h):
    return m*(side(m,h)+b[1]*g+b[2]*g**2+b[3]*g**3)
def bis(f,lo,hi,*a):
    for _ in range(100):
        mid=(lo+hi)/2
        if f(lo,*a)*f(mid,*a)<=0: hi=mid
        else: lo=mid
    return (lo+hi)/2
def solve(pH):
    h=10**-pH
    # try solid present: m fixed by Ksp
    m=Ks*h*h; lg=bis(gly_balance,-20,-1.9,m,h); g=10**lg
    if ni_diss(m,g,h) < NT:
        solid=True
    else:
        solid=False
        def f(lm):
            m=10**lm; lg=bis(gly_balance,-20,-1.9,m,h); return ni_diss(m,10**lg,h)-NT
        lm=bis(f,-40,0); m=10**lm; lg=bis(gly_balance,-20,-1.9,m,h); g=10**lg
    sp={'Ni2+':m,'NiOH+':m*KOH/h,'Ni(OH)3-':m*K3/h**3,
        'NiGly+':m*b[1]*g,'NiGly2':m*b[2]*g**2,'NiGly3-':m*b[3]*g**3}
    sp['Ni(OH)2(s)'] = NT-sum(sp.values()) if solid else 0.0
    return m,g,sp

pHs=np.arange(0,14.001,0.01)
recs=[solve(p) for p in pHs]
mfree=np.array([r[0] for r in recs]); gfree=np.array([r[1] for r in recs])
names=list(recs[0][2].keys())
dom=[max(r[2],key=r[2].get) for r in recs]
E_low = E0_Ni + 0.05916/2*np.log10(mfree)
E_up  = E0_NiOOH - 0.05916*np.log10(mfree) - 3*0.05916*pHs

# report
print("Species predominance (Ni(II) domain):")
cur=dom[0]; start=pHs[0]
for p,d in zip(pHs,dom):
    if d!=cur: print(f"  {cur:12s} pH {start:5.2f} - {p:5.2f}"); cur=d; start=p
print(f"  {cur:12s} pH {start:5.2f} - {pHs[-1]:5.2f}")
for p in [0,2,4,6,8,10,11,12,13,14]:
    i=int(round(p/0.01)); r=recs[i][2]
    print(f"pH {p:2d}: free Ni2+ {mfree[i]:.2e} M, free Gly- {gfree[i]:.2e} M, E(Ni/NiII)={E_low[i]:+.3f} V, E(NiII/NiOOH)={E_up[i]:+.3f} V, "
          + ", ".join(f"{k} {v/NT*100:.0f}%" for k,v in r.items() if v/NT>0.01))

# ---- plot ----
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,6.5),dpi=150)
cols={'Ni2+':'#cfe8f3','NiOH+':'#b0d0e8','Ni(OH)3-':'#9fb8d8','NiGly+':'#d9f0c8','NiGly2':'#a9dc8f',
      'NiGly3-':'#79c46a','Ni(OH)2(s)':'#e6d3b3'}
lab={'Ni2+':'Ni$^{2+}$','NiOH+':'NiOH$^+$','Ni(OH)3-':'Ni(OH)$_3^-$','NiGly+':'Ni(Gly)$^+$',
     'NiGly2':'Ni(Gly)$_2^0$','NiGly3-':'Ni(Gly)$_3^-$','Ni(OH)2(s)':'Ni(OH)$_2$(s)'}
ax.fill_between(pHs,-1.2,E_low,color='#bfbfbf',label='Ni(s)')
ax.fill_between(pHs,E_up,2.2,color='#3b3b3b',label='NiOOH(s)')
used=[]
cur=dom[0]; i0=0
for i in range(1,len(pHs)+1):
    if i==len(pHs) or dom[i]!=cur:
        sl=slice(i0,i); ax.fill_between(pHs[sl],E_low[sl],E_up[sl],color=cols[cur])
        pm=0.5*(pHs[i0]+pHs[i-1]); k=(i0+i)//2
        ax.text(pm,0.5*(E_low[k]+E_up[k]),lab[cur],ha='center',va='center',fontsize=9,rotation=0)
        if cur not in used: used.append(cur)
        if i<len(pHs): ax.vlines(pHs[i],E_low[i],E_up[i],color='k',lw=0.8); cur=dom[i]; i0=i
ax.plot(pHs,E_low,'k',lw=1); ax.plot(pHs,E_up,'k',lw=1)
ax.plot(pHs,1.229-0.05916*pHs,'k--',lw=0.9); ax.plot(pHs,-0.05916*pHs,'k--',lw=0.9)
ax.text(0.3,1.15,'O$_2$/H$_2$O',fontsize=8); ax.text(0.3,-0.1,'H$^+$/H$_2$',fontsize=8)
ax.text(7,-0.9,'Ni(s)',ha='center',fontsize=11); ax.text(7,1.8,'NiOOH(s)',ha='center',fontsize=11,color='w')
ax.set_xlim(0,14); ax.set_ylim(-1.2,2.2); ax.set_xlabel('pH'); ax.set_ylabel('E / V vs SHE')
ax.set_title('Ni–glycine–H$_2$O Pourbaix diagram: 1 mM Ni, 10 mM glycine, 25 °C, I = 0.1 m')
ax.legend(handles=[Patch(color=cols[k],label=lab[k]) for k in used],loc='upper right',fontsize=8,title='Ni(II) predominant')
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('/mnt/user-data/outputs/Ni_glycine_pourbaix.png')
np.savetxt('/mnt/user-data/outputs/Ni_glycine_pourbaix_boundaries.csv',
           np.c_[pHs,mfree,gfree,E_low,E_up],delimiter=',',header='pH,free_Ni2+_M,free_Gly-_M,E_Ni/NiII_V,E_NiII/NiOOH_V',comments='',fmt='%.4e')

import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ---------------- conditions ----------------
T=298.15; F=96485.33; R=8.314462; RTF=R*T/F*np.log(10)   # 0.05916 V
CuT=1.00e-3; NT=0.100; Eh=0.265; I=0.1
# Davies
A=0.509; sI=np.sqrt(I); f=A*(sI/(1+sI)-0.3*I)
g=lambda z: 10**(-f*z*z) if z!=0 else 10**(0.1*I)   # neutral species: log g = 0.1 I
g0,g1,g2=g(0),g(1),g(2)
Kw=10**-13.997; Ka=10**-9.244            # NH4+ -> NH3 + H+ (I=0)
# Cu(II) hydrolysis, IUPAC (Powell et al. 2007), I=0:  Cu2+ + nH2O -> Cu(OH)n + nH+
lb=dict(b1=-7.95,b2=-16.2,b3=-26.6,b4=-39.7,b22=-10.43)
# Cu(II)-NH3 stepwise (NIST 46, I=0.1): logK 4.15,3.50,2.89,2.13
bII=np.cumsum([4.15,3.50,2.89,2.13]); bII=10**bII
# Cu(I)-NH3 (I=0.1): log b1 5.93, log b2 10.86
bI=10**np.array([5.93,10.86])
E0=0.153                                   # Cu2+/Cu+
r=10**(-(Eh-E0)/RTF)                       # a(Cu+)/a(Cu2+)
logK_hyd=8.64      # Cu(OH)2(s) + 2H+ = Cu2+ + 2H2O   (Baes & Mesmer)
logK_cu2o=-1.55    # Cu2O(s) + 2H+ = 2Cu+ + H2O       (NBS Gf)
E0_CuI_Cu=0.521    # Cu+ + e- = Cu

def solve(pH):
    h=10**-pH; oh=Kw/h
    def dissolved(aN):
        # Cu(II) linear factor (conc = a_Cu2+ * F2)
        F2=1/g2 + sum(bII[n-1]*aN**n for n in range(1,5))/g2 \
           + 10**lb['b1']/h/g1 + 10**lb['b2']/h**2/g0 + 10**lb['b3']/h**3/g1 + 10**lb['b4']/h**4/g2
        F1=r*(1+bI[0]*aN+bI[1]*aN**2)/g1
        D=2*10**lb['b22']/h**2/g2          # dimer term: D*x^2
        a=D; b=F2+F1; c=-CuT
        xfree=(-b+np.sqrt(b*b-4*a*c))/(2*a) if a>0 else CuT/b
        cap_h=10**logK_hyd*h*h
        cap_o=np.sqrt(10**logK_cu2o)*h/r
        x=min(xfree,cap_h,cap_o)
        solid='none'
        if x<xfree: solid='Cu(OH)2' if cap_h<=cap_o else 'Cu2O'
        return x,F2,F1,D,solid
    def resid(logaN):
        aN=10**logaN; x,F2,F1,D,_=dissolved(aN)
        cuII_am=sum(n*bII[n-1]*aN**n for n in range(1,5))*x/g2
        cuI_am=r*x*(bI[0]*aN+2*bI[1]*aN**2)/g1
        return aN/g0 + aN*h/Ka/g1 + cuII_am + cuI_am - NT
    lo,hi=-25,np.log10(NT)+0.1
    for _ in range(200):
        mid=(lo+hi)/2
        if resid(mid)>0: hi=mid
        else: lo=mid
    aN=10**((lo+hi)/2); x,F2,F1,D,solid=dissolved(aN)
    c={}
    c['Cu2+']=x/g2
    for n in range(1,5): c[f'Cu(NH3){n}2+']=bII[n-1]*aN**n*x/g2
    c['CuOH+']=10**lb['b1']*x/h/g1; c['Cu(OH)2(aq)']=10**lb['b2']*x/h**2/g0
    c['Cu(OH)3-']=10**lb['b3']*x/h**3/g1; c['Cu(OH)4 2-']=10**lb['b4']*x/h**4/g2
    c['Cu2(OH)2 2+ (as Cu)']=2*10**lb['b22']*x*x/h**2/g2
    c['Cu+']=r*x/g1; c['Cu(NH3)+']=r*x*bI[0]*aN/g1; c['Cu(NH3)2+']=r*x*bI[1]*aN**2/g1
    diss=sum(c.values())
    c['Cu(OH)2(s)']=CuT-diss if solid=='Cu(OH)2' else 0.0
    c['Cu2O(s) (as Cu)']=CuT-diss if solid=='Cu2O' else 0.0
    # Cu metal check: a_Cu+ vs equilibrium activity at Eh
    aCu_eq=10**((Eh-E0_CuI_Cu)/RTF)
    return c, aN, r*x/aCu_eq

pHs=np.linspace(0,14,701)
rows=[]; names=None; satCu=[]; freeN=[]
for p in pHs:
    c,aN,s=solve(p); names=list(c); rows.append([c[k] for k in names]); satCu.append(s); freeN.append(aN)
M=np.array(rows); satCu=np.array(satCu)
print("max a(Cu+)/a(Cu+)eq for Cu(s):",satCu.max(),"-> Cu metal", "stable somewhere" if satCu.max()>1 else "never stable")
# boundaries
dom=[names[i] for i in M.argmax(1)]
prev=None
for p,d in zip(pHs,dom):
    if d!=prev: print(f"pH {p:5.2f}: dominant -> {d}"); prev=d
for i,k in enumerate(names):
    m=M[:,i].max()
    print(f"{k:24s} max frac {m/CuT:8.3e} at pH {pHs[M[:,i].argmax()]:.2f}")
np.savetxt("/mnt/user-data/outputs/cu_nh3_speciation.csv",np.column_stack([pHs,freeN,M]),delimiter=",",
           header="pH,free_NH3_activity,"+",".join(names),comments="")

# ---------- plot ----------
fig,ax=plt.subplots(2,1,figsize=(9,10),sharex=True)
cols=plt.cm.tab20(np.linspace(0,1,len(names)))
for i,k in enumerate(names):
    fr=M[:,i]/CuT
    if fr.max()<0.01: continue
    ls='--' if k in ('Cu+','Cu(NH3)+','Cu(NH3)2+') else ('-' if '(s)' not in k else ':')
    lw=2.5 if '(s)' in k else 1.6
    ax[0].plot(pHs,fr,ls,color=cols[i],lw=lw,label=k)
    ax[1].plot(pHs,np.log10(np.maximum(M[:,i],1e-30)),ls,color=cols[i],lw=lw,label=k)
ax[0].set_ylabel("fraction of total Cu"); ax[0].set_ylim(0,1.02); ax[0].grid(alpha=.3)
ax[0].set_title(f"Cu speciation: Cu_T = {CuT:.2e} M, NH3_T = {NT:.3f} M, Eh = +{Eh:.3f} V (SHE), 25 °C, I = {I} m\n"
                "solids allowed: Cu(OH)2(s), Cu2O(s), Cu(s); dashed = Cu(I), dotted = solids",fontsize=10)
ax[0].legend(fontsize=7.5,ncol=3,loc='center left')
ax[1].set_ylim(-9,-2.5); ax[1].set_ylabel("log [species] (M)"); ax[1].set_xlabel("pH"); ax[1].grid(alpha=.3)
ax[1].set_xticks(range(0,15))
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("/mnt/user-data/outputs/cu_nh3_speciation.png",dpi=160)
